title: poki: an MCP server that drives a real iPhone

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: The catch: it controls your real iPhone, so the screen goes to your model service. And you need a Mac with Xcode.

scenes.heading: CAN POKI USE YOUR IPHONE?
scenes.say: Ever wanted AI to use your iPhone for you?

scenes.heading: RUNS ON YOUR MAC
scenes.say: It's called Poki, it's open source, and it runs on your Mac. Clone it, run the setup script, then start it.

scenes.heading: YOUR AGENT, YOUR PLAN
scenes.say: Then add it to Claude Code or Codex as an MCP server, so your own subscription drives the phone.

scenes.heading: ONE TASK, REAL TAPS
scenes.say: Give it a task, like searching the web in Chrome and summarizing the top result. It taps and types for real.

scenes.heading: FASTER THE SECOND TIME
scenes.say: It remembers past tasks, so the same job runs faster the second time.

scenes.heading: THE CATCH
scenes.say: The catch: it controls your real iPhone, so the screen goes to your model service. And you need a Mac with Xcode.
Would you hand your phone to an agent? Comment IPHONE and I'll pin the repo.

viewer.who: developers and tinkerers who want their agent to reach their phone
viewer.problem: agents stop at the desktop; a phone needs taps, not API calls
viewer.job: decide whether a phone-driving agent is worth setting up on a Mac

idea: Poki is a local MCP server that lets a coding agent read and act on a real iPhone screen.

claims.text: Open source and local: clone the repo, run ./bin/setup, then npm start on a Mac.
Register it as an MCP server in Claude Code or Codex and use your own subscription.
Its tools tap, type and scroll a real screen; the README's example task searches Chrome and summarizes.
Poki Agent remembers past tasks and runs them faster on repeat.
